title: Codex as a principal: nsh-agent
summary: bin/nsh-agent.rex (kit: /opt/newshell/bin/nsh-agent): describe (the brief an LLM is given), check FILE (the check plus the source of every method FILE calls), run FILE [--follows JOB] [--wait S] (runs as the config principal, default codex, waits for submitted jobs, prints each report), jobs, report JOB. stdout is for the agent, progress on stderr; exit 0 ok, 1 a job FAILED/DIED, 2 rejected/refused/error. Agent is a ShellContext with no LLM client. A JobStore keeps each settled job as JSON in the state directory and every invocation restores them, so jobs~find, amend and History work across separate commands. Plan steps run as their owner's principal.
authority: built and tested (architecture Tom Dyer; coding and writing Claude (Opus 5.5), 2026-11-24)
invariants: Codex works one command at a time; nothing it needs may live only in one process
Plan steps run as the principal that owns the plan
Codex reads the report from run; it never polls a build
procedure: Write the proposal to a file, nsh-agent check it, then nsh-agent run it; answer a stopped job with --follows JOBNAME

provenance.claim: the killed-compile chain as separate processes; refusals; objects
